sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and stylesheet
sections.what: Brings in the page type definitions and loads the shared stylesheet so the style rules apply to every page.
sections.why: Loading the shared stylesheet here is how the styles reach every page.
sections.watch_out: Removing this import leaves every page unstyled.

sections.name: metadata
sections.title: Site title and install settings
sections.what: Sets the browser tab title to CareerOS, a short description, the app manifest for home screen install, and turns off phone number highlighting.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app be added to a phone home screen and look like an app.
sections.watch_out: The manifest path includes a repository name, so a different hosting path breaks installation.

sections.name: viewport
sections.title: Screen settings and early theme script
sections.what: Sets screen scaling, theme colors for light and dark mode, and holds the small script that picks the theme before the page is drawn.
sections.why: The script runs early so the page does not flash the wrong theme, as its comment states.
sections.watch_out: The script is stored in the viewport section, so it is easy to miss when editing the theme setup.

sections.name: RootLayout
sections.title: Page wrapper
sections.what: Wraps every page in the HTML and body tags, adds the icon link and the early theme script, and sets light as the default theme.
sections.why: Every page needs this outer shell.
sections.watch_out: The hardcoded light default is only a fallback, because the early script changes it before paint.

summary: The outer frame for every page of CareerOS. It sets the page title, install settings, screen settings, and a small script that picks light or dark theme before the page is drawn.
purpose: Gives every page the same frame, title and theme.
why: Likely reason: the framework needs one root layout, and the theme script sits here so it runs before the page appears, avoiding a flash of the wrong theme.
how: 1. The stylesheet is loaded. 2. Title and install settings are read by the framework. 3. Screen and theme color settings are read. 4. The page wrapper adds the icon link and the theme script, sets the default theme to light, and places the page content inside the body.
inputs: The page content passed in, the theme saved in the browser, and the system light or dark preference.
outputs: A complete HTML page with its title, theme color, install details and the chosen theme set before the first paint.
risks: The icon and manifest paths include a repository name prefix, so they break if the site is hosted at a different path. The theme script depends on a storage key name that must match other files. If the script fails, the page falls back to light.
debug: If the wrong theme shows, check the saved theme value in browser storage and the theme script. If the page has no styles, check the stylesheet import. If the install icon or manifest fails on a new host, check the path prefix.
